issued_by.impersonation_disclaimer: Not a human reviewer and not the owner.

part_1_f12_result.not_load: reproduced standalone at load 5.7 in 17m, and again under a widened 600s checkpoint timeout: ordinals 1 and 2 checkpoint instantly, ordinal 3 never checkpoints. The 10-second timeout is not the cause.

part_2_root_cause_confirmed.mechanism: epoch-6 keeps the primary-container fingerprint as a recursive _tree_fingerprint (rglob plus per-file sha256) of the whole container, which nests PRIMARY-LEDGER and MIRROR-RECEIPTS, and keeps registered_v2_2_secondary_snapshots as a recursive fingerprint of the snapshot root. The snapshot root accumulates one full byte-for-byte ledger copy per sealed ordinal, and the container grows with the ledger. _real_path_fingerprints, which hashes all eleven scopes recursively, is called many times per attempt, several before the started checkpoint is persisted.
part_2_root_cause_confirmed.consequence: per-attempt fingerprint cost grows with the number of prior sealed ordinals and the accumulating snapshot copies. By ordinal 3 the pre-checkpoint fingerprinting over two accumulated full-ledger snapshots plus the grown container exceeds even a 600-second window, so the child never reaches started_persisted.
part_2_root_cause_confirmed.evidence: the ordinal-3 child spawned about 880 seconds into the fixture and sampled in module import then select_poll_poll, the signature of heavy sequential subprocess and filesystem work; two through-ordinal snapshots were present under the secondary snapshot root; _tree_fingerprint rglobs the entire subtree.
part_2_root_cause_confirmed.why_attempt_1_did_not_show_it: the official attempt 1 sealed a single failed ordinal and stopped; only a multi-ordinal series, which exists solely in this fixture, accumulates enough snapshots to blow the budget. Same F-16 class: the cost interaction lives in a path only the multi-ordinal exact-OS test exercises.

part_3_finding_F17.title: Recursive fingerprints over accumulating snapshot copies make per-attempt cost superlinear in sealed ordinals
part_3_finding_F17.detail: durable-evidence mirroring copies the full ledger every ordinal and the epoch-6 scope set fingerprints those copies recursively on every _real_path_fingerprints call. Correctness is fine; cost is not.
part_3_finding_F17.note: the 10-second checkpoint timeout is a separate fragility (recorded but not the cause) and must not be treated as the fix

part_4_fix_direction_for_r2.principle: the positive-transition and immutability checks care only about the ACTIVE ledger subtree and whether non-ledger scopes are unchanged; they do not need to re-hash immutable already-sealed snapshots on every call
options_for_the_operator_to_choose_and_j: fingerprint the accumulating snapshot and receipt scopes by a cheap stable summary, for example a directory-entry-name and per-immutable-snapshot recorded-root manifest, rather than a full recursive byte re-hash on every call, since each through-ordinal snapshot is create-only and its root is already recorded at mirror time
or scope the hot pre-checkpoint fingerprint to exactly the keys the transition predicate consumes, computing the full recursive form only where an equality span genuinely requires it
either way preserve every correctness property: key set self-check, ancestor-projection equality, seal-then-mirror, and tamper detection over the active ledger and its container
part_4_fix_direction_for_r2.must_not: do not fix this by widening the test timeout or by trimming what the mirror copies; the mirror's full copy is the durability guarantee and stays
part_4_fix_direction_for_r2.test_requirement: the exact-OS multi-ordinal fixture must run to SUCCESS at ordinal 3 within a sane bound, and a registered assertion must bound per-attempt fingerprint work so a future superlinear regression fails fast rather than at F-12
part_4_fix_direction_for_r2.surface: scripts/p4_2a_v2_2_heldout_rehearsal.py and tests/test_p4_2a_v2_2_heldout_rehearsal_runner.py; r2 as a new direct child of the SAME authority 3ccc2f2; fc156f07 stays in history
